name: Foreground service timeouts (Android 15)
plain: Some foreground services now stop after 6 hours in 24, and can only restart after a user returns to the app.
meaning: A hard cap on long background syncs and media processing. It limits always-running services; Android 17 adds memory and audio limits on top.

android.persistence: dataSync and mediaProcessing get 6 hours total per 24 h; timer resets when the app is brought to the foreground
android.api_surface: Service.onTimeout(int, int); startForeground throws ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException when exhausted
android.note: Service gets a few seconds after onTimeout to call stopSelf() or a RemoteServiceException is thrown; shortService limit about 3 min

ios.note: iOS has no foreground service; background modes have no fixed daily cap but suspension is immediate once work ends

limits.headline: Can keep some Android services running, but only about 6 hours in 24
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when an app runs a long sync or media job in the background
can: Keep a long sync or media job going for several hours at a stretch
Restart a stopped service once you open the app again
Use a short service for quick tasks, which gets about 3 minutes
cannot: Run a data sync service past the daily limit without you opening the app
Keep working after the system calls time out; the app gets only a few seconds to stop
Do this on iPhone, which has no foreground services and suspends apps as soon as work ends
limits.reach_label: Hard daily time limit on Android 15
limits.differs: Android 15 caps some long services. iPhone has no such service type and simply suspends apps when work ends.

story.what_it_is: Android now stops some always-running background tasks after about 6 hours in a day.

marketing.name: Foreground service timeouts
marketing.pitch: Android 15 puts a time limit on certain long-running background services so apps cannot drain the battery all day.

story.for_you: You never see it work. Your phone just stops apps from quietly running heavy tasks for hours, so your battery lasts longer. If an app was syncing a huge backup, it may pause until you open it again.
story.for_makers: Makers must design long jobs to finish, save progress and resume. It forces them to move big uploads and media work to smarter tools instead of one endless service.

use_cases.example: A video editor exporting a long 4K clip keeps going in the background, then must pause and resume if the export runs past the daily limit.
A running tracker that keeps a data sync service alive all day must now finish cleanly and restart when you next open it.
A big game download or patch in the background gets paused near the limit and resumes when you return to the game.
A cloud drive uploading thousands of photos overnight switches to scheduled jobs so it is not killed by the timeout.
A health app that copies sensor data from a watch all day has to batch the data instead of running nonstop.
A delivery company app that polled for new orders in the background now relies on push messages instead.

risks: Background jobs can stop mid task
Sync may lag until you reopen the app
story.android_note: Applies from Android 15. The app gets a few seconds to wrap up when the timer fires, or it crashes.
story.ios_note: iOS has no equivalent. Apps are simply put to sleep soon after their work ends.

technical_bounds: Applies to apps targeting 35 and above

history.change: 6 hour per 24 h timeout for dataSync and mediaProcessing (targetSdk 35)
